row.prior_work: **Predicts T > 0; silent on the 6.3 bar and on cross-run noise as its cause.** Tsui 2025, Self-Correction Bench (arXiv 2507.02778 v3; Claude 3.5 Haiku 52.5%, Sonnet 4 41.4% blind spot) and Khullar, Hopkins, Wang and Roger 2026, Self-Attribution Bias (arXiv 2603.04582; Claude 3.5 Haiku, Sonnet 4, Opus 4.1): text in the model's own assistant turn is let off more than the same text in a user turn, which predicts a positive T in any run. On the noise that this test removes: JudgeSense (Bellibatlu, Raff and Zhang 2026, arXiv 2604.23478 v3) finds LLM judges disagree with themselves on identical prompts, most on graded tasks (Claude Haiku 4.5 coherence −0.206 against its own repeats), and Zhao, Esmaeili and Fard 2026 (arXiv 2604.16790) report two-run consistency of 70–90%; both predict noise of unknown sign, not a direction (`map/reads/remap-2026-11-05b-sg-b4.md`). No paper tests whether a quoted copy's leniency gap survives a same-run comparison. What this bet adds: sg-b4's comparison with every cell graded in one run, Haiku twice, on the 5.5 models, which removes the cross-run confound its audit named. The engine's 16 sits below the papers' direction because the rule needs Haiku's mean to clear a bar its sg-b4 median (5.5) did not.
row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that same-run own-turn penalties come out larger than sg-b3's archived ones, shrinking Haiku's T to between 0 and 6.3: sg-b4's half-point margin was cross-run luck.

row.lesson: "Correcting P8, P10: sg-b4 compared quoted grades with own-turn grades from an earlier run, and Haiku's pass rested on a half-point margin and one domain. This bet grades all four cells in one run, Haiku twice each, and reports median and domain drops, and its odds are 16% (map: none) because under-$1, literature and layer-4 rows run low."

row.prior_work: **Mixed; no lead-in-only test in print.** JudgeSense (Bellibatlu, Raff and Zhang 2026, arXiv 2604.23478 v3): rewording a judge's instruction while keeping its question moves graded verdicts beyond repeat noise (pooled coherence −0.181), direction unstated, which predicts S ≠ 0 of unknown sign. Grossmann and Kross 2014 (Psychological Science 25:1571; adults): a third-person, distancing wording shrank a human self-other gap in reasoning, which predicts that the deictic "Now grade the conclusion above" keeps part of the own-turn frame (S > 0). Khullar, Hopkins, Wang and Roger 2026 (arXiv 2603.04582; Claude 3.5 Haiku, Sonnet 4, Opus 4.1): explicit authorship wording moves leniency by 0.5 of 10 or less, which predicts a small S. Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv 2606.05976 v2; Qwen2.5-72B, math): a label-free boundary carried part of the gain from moving a claim out of the model's own turn and the role tag the rest, which predicts that structure, not one line, carries most of it. Read in `map/reads/remap-2026-11-05b-sg-b4.md`. What this bet adds: the first split of sg-b4's remainder that changes one line only, on the 5.5 models, with both lead-ins graded in one run. The engine's 14 sits below a mixed prior because both Haiku and Opus must clear their bars, and Opus's 0.75 bar sits on a 1.5-point remainder over 30 studies (the dry run: Opus passes under half the time even if the lead-in carries all of it).
row.premortem: If this fails, the most likely reason is that Opus's S on 30 studies lands between 0 and 0.75 or its cluster interval reaches below 0: a 1.5-point remainder is too small to split at this n.

fields.prior_work: **Mixed; the nearest closing-line-only test predicts a small S of either sign.** Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv 2606.05976 v2, §4.4 and §4.5; Qwen2.5-72B, math): with a wrong claim left in the model's own assistant-turn <thought> block, changing only the trailing instruction moved explicit correction from 16.7% to between 0.0% and 33.3%, in both directions, while relabeling the claim's role reached 70.0%: a closing line moves the outcome less than structure does, and either way. JudgeSense (Bellibatlu, Raff and Zhang 2026, arXiv 2604.23478 v3): rewording a judge's instruction while keeping its question moves graded verdicts beyond repeat noise (pooled coherence −0.181), direction unstated. Khullar, Hopkins, Wang and Roger 2026 (arXiv 2603.04582; Claude 3.5 Haiku, Sonnet 4, Opus 4.1): explicit authorship statements move leniency within 0.5 of 10, i.e. up to 5 of 100, above both bars here, and they concern authorship, not a lead-in, so they bound S loosely and do not predict a miss. Grossmann and Kross 2014 (Psychological Science 25:1571): a third-person, distancing wording shrank a human self-other gap; an analogy only, since neither closing line refers to the self. Fox, Caspy and Reisler 1994 (found by the design review's search; abstract only): a cautionary instruction did not reduce human self-rating leniency, while changes to the rating scale and form did. What this bet adds over Chen: the first closing-line-only swap on a graded penalty for a planted overclaim, in a quoted User/Assistant transcript of the model's own conversation, on Claude 5.5 models, with both lines graded in one run. Why the engine's 14: the nearest test (Chen §4.4, §4.5) found closing-instruction changes small and of either sign beside structural changes, both Haiku and Opus must clear their bars, and Opus's 0.75 bar sits on a 1.5-point remainder over 30 studies.
